blocks.en: Train and held-out test phases, and innovate and improve modes, keep separate coefficients because they measure different experimental objects. Within each published setting, the leaderboard reports the mean paper score over published papers. The scale comes from the reference cohort, and FNI is this score scaled by 100: a paper’s typical score across the cohort has magnitude 100, so a model that matches the cohort scores about 100, a model with about half again as much improvement scores near 150 150 , and a model at half the cohort’s gains scores near 50 50 ; the score is positive when the model improves over the source reproduction and negative when it regresses. Because each paper’s spread across the cohort is about one, averaging over many published papers shrinks the noise in a model’s mean score, so models are separated by the average of many per-paper differences rather than by any single paper; we therefore read only sustained gaps as real and treat very close scores as ties. A paper is excluded from publication uniformly for every model, never per submission, when the cohort gives no usable scale (every cell tied, or a baseline that cancels to zero) or is too small to estimate spread (fewer than three cohort models present).
blocks.zh: 训练和停产试验阶段,以及创新和改进模式,保持单独的系数,因为它们测量不同的实验物体。 在每个公布的设定中,领导板报告平均论文得分高于公布的论文. 比例表来自参考组,FNI是这个分数的100:一个论文在组的典型分数有100级,因此一个模型与组的分数相匹配,一个模型的分数大约是150分左右的改进分数的一半,一个模型的分数大约是50分左右;当模型在源头复制上有所改进时,得分是正数,当模型倒退时为负数。 因为每篇论文的分布范围大约是一篇,平均超过许多出版的论文缩小了模型平均分数中的噪音,所以模型以许多纸面差异的平均值而不是任何单一的论文来分隔;因此,我们只把持续的差距看成是真实的,把非常接近的分数当作联系。 当组群没有给出可用的尺度(每个单元格捆绑,或一个取消为零的基线)或太小,无法估计分布(低于现有三个组群模型)时,每一份模型都统一不公布。

blocks.en: Appendix F Evaluation Analysis
blocks.zh: 附录F 评价分析

blocks.en: The main text reads these environments as a leaderboard. Here we examine the evaluation behind it, asking three questions: how often a scientist actually improves on the reproduced method, whether a score reflects a real gain rather than a metric optimized during the run, and whether the number is largely a proxy for how much compute or interaction a run was given. In short: usually, yes, and no.
blocks.zh: 主文将这些环境解读为领导板. 这里我们研究了它背后的评价,提出了三个问题:一个科学家在复制的方法上实际改进的频率是多少,一个分数是否反映了真正的收益而不是运行期间的度量优化,以及这个数字是否在很大程度上是计算或交互运行给出的代名词. 简而言之:通常是,是,也不是。

blocks.en: F.1 How Often Scientists Beat the Paper
blocks.zh: F.1 科学家的频繁程度 击败纸

blocks.en: Before asking which scientist is best, it is worth knowing whether any of them do real work. They do. Figure 35 shows the distribution of held-out improvement over the paper’s source method, one panel per mode. Most runs land to the right of zero: 84% beat the reproduced method when improving it, and 74% do when designing a new one from scratch. Innovate carries the heavier left tail, since a fresh design more often fails outright, yet even there the typical attempt still moves the metric forward.
blocks.zh: 在问到哪个科学家是最好的之前,值得知道他们中是否有人真正工作. 没错 图35显示与纸张来源方法(每个模式一个面板)相比被搁置的改进分布情况。 大部分土地为零:84%在改良时比照复制方法,74%在设计新方法时从零开始。 创新型搭载着较重的左尾,因为新的设计更经常彻底失败,但即使在那里,典型的尝试仍然将公尺向前移动.

blocks.en: Figure 35 : How often scientists beat the paper. Distribution of held-out improvement over the paper’s source method, per mode. Colored bars (right of zero) beat the reproduced method; the grey tail regressed. The percentage is the share of runs that improved.
blocks.zh: 图35:科学家如何经常打报纸。 按方式分发对纸张来源方法的搁置改进。 彩色条(零的右)击败复制的方法;灰尾退后. 百分比是运行中有所改善的份额。

blocks.en: F.2 Do the Gains Generalize
blocks.zh: F.2 收益普遍化

blocks.en: A score is only meaningful if it reflects a real gain rather than a metric gamed during the run. The held-out split separates the two: a scientist optimizes against a training-phase metric but is scored on a test slice it never sees. Figure 36 plots one against the other. The two track closely (Spearman 0.57 0.57 in improve and 0.69 0.69 in innovate), so training gains usually survive to the held-out metric, and only a small share of runs fall in the overfit quadrant where a training gain reverses on test (8% in improve and 5% in innovate). The split rarely needs to intervene, but when it does it removes exactly the runs that would otherwise inflate a score.
blocks.zh: 一个分数只有在反映实际收益而不是在跑步期间的衡量游戏时才有意义. 被搁置的分裂将两者分开:一位科学家对照训练阶段的度量标准进行优化,但在它从未看到的试验片上得分。 图36是一对一。 两条赛道(Spearman 0.57 0.57 改进和0.69 0.69 革新)紧密相连,因此培训收益通常能维持到被搁置的衡量标准,而且只有一小部分跑道在过于适合的象限中下降,在这种象限中,训练在测试中反转(8%改进和5%革新)。 分数很少需要干预,但当分数完成时,它完全消除了本来会给分数增高的运行.

blocks.en: Figure 36 : Training gains carry over to held-out test. Training-phase score against held-out test score, per mode, with the y = x y=x line. Points hug the diagonal; the shaded quadrant holds the few runs that gained on training but regressed on test.
blocks.zh: 图36:培训成果转入搁置测试。 训练阶段分数对照停赛测试分数,每模式,y=×××线. 点紧抱对角线;荫影四角线紧握着在训练上获得但测试后倒退的少数跑步.

blocks.en: F.3 Effort and Outcomes
blocks.zh: F.3 努力和成果

blocks.en: A natural worry is that a score mostly tracks how much compute or interaction a run spent, rewarding brute force over insight. It does not. Figure 37 plots each run’s within-paper normalized score against the GPU-hours it consumed and the number of turns it took, with the Improve and Innovate modes kept apart. Every trend is flat: the rank correlation stays weak throughout and is slightly negative where it moves at all, at most 0.22 0.22 in magnitude. Spending more does not produce a better result; a better method does.
blocks.zh: 一个自然的担忧是,一个分数主要跟踪 计算或互动 花费,奖励野蛮的力量 而不是洞察力。 它没有。 图37 图37显示每个运行的纸内正常分数与所消耗的GPU时数和转弯次数, 每一种趋势都是平的:军衔关联在整个过程中一直很弱,在运动时略微呈负值,最多0.22 0.22级。 花费更多资金不会产生更好的结果;更好的方法确实如此。

blocks.en: Figure 37 : Effort versus outcome. Within-paper normalized score against GPU-hours (top row) and agent turns (bottom row), shown separately for the Improve and Innovate modes. Scores are min-max normalized within each (paper, mode); each line is a least-squares fit in log-effort. Every panel is flat ( | ρ | ≤ 0.22 |\rho|\leq 0.22 ).
blocks.zh: 图37:努力与结果。 纸内比对GPU小时(上行)和代理转弯(下行)的正常得分,分别显示在改进和创新模式上. 分数在每个(纸张,模式)内是分数的常态化;每行是最小的方位,适合日志操作. 每个面板都是平的(| ρ ρ 0.22 |\rho|\leq 0.22 ).

blocks.en: Appendix G Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 附录G 实验 设置

blocks.en: This section records the concrete setup behind our experiments: the paper set the scientists attempt, the compute pool they run on, the agent scaffolds and models we compare, and how trials are run and scored.
blocks.zh: 本节记录了我们实验背后的具体布局: 论文设定了科学家的尝试, 他们运行的计算池, 代理脚手架和模型, 我们比较, 以及试验是如何运行和得分的。

blocks.en: G.1 Data
blocks.zh: G.1 数据

blocks.en: All papers come from arXiv. We work from a global index of 124,816 unique papers in the categories cs.CL, cs.CV, cs.AI, and cs.LG, built from daily listings between January 1, 2025 and March 1, 2026 and exported on March 28, 2026. From this index, the selection procedure of § D chooses a category-balanced set of 1,000 papers to attempt; the per-stage counts are reported there.
blocks.zh: 所有文件都来自ArXiv。 我们的工作来自全球指数124,816份Cs.CL,cs.CV,cs.AI,和cs.LG等类别的独特论文,由2025年1月1日至2026年3月1日的每日上市所建立,2026年3月28日出口. 从这一指数中,§D的筛选程序选择了一组1000份论文的分类平衡,以便尝试;每个阶段的计数报告在那里.

blocks.en: G.2 Compute
blocks.zh: G.2 计算

blocks.en: ’s experiments run on a heterogeneous setup provisioned through Hive and accounted by Nexus. The compute pool contains 16 A100 GPU nodes, 16 H100 GPU nodes, 16 H200 GPU nodes, and 4 CPU nodes (Table 13 ). The GPU nodes support accelerator-heavy reproduction jobs, while the CPU nodes support CPU-only experiments and non-accelerated setup or validation work.
blocks.zh: 由Nexus负责。 计算池包含16个A100 GPU节点,16个H100 GPU节点,16个H200 GPU节点,以及4个CPU节点(表13). GPU节点支持加速器-重力复制任务,而CPU节点则支持CPU唯一的实验和不加速的设置或验证工作.

blocks.en: Table 13 : Hive exposes heterogeneous capacity for accelerator-heavy and CPU-only experiments. The counts describe the compute capacity exposed in Hive.
blocks.zh: 表13:蜂窝暴露出加速器-重力实验和只使用CPU实验的不同能力. 计数描述在蜂巢中暴露的计算能力.

blocks.en: G.3 Agent Scaffolds
blocks.zh: G.3 代理脚手架

blocks.en: Each scientist reaches the workspace through a scaffold, the layer that drives a coding-agent command-line tool behind one uniform turn interface (§ A.4 ). Our experiments center on two scaffolds: Claude Code, which runs Anthropic models, and Codex, which runs OpenAI models. The same harness also supports other agents, including Gemini, Kimi, and Grok, so a single task can be run across a range of models. We prioritize a provider’s official agent scaffold when one is released; otherwise we use Claude Code as the default. Because a model and its scaffold are evaluated together and not every model runs through the same scaffold, the unit being compared is a model together with its scaffold, and a scaffold difference is part of what the comparison measures rather than something controlled away.
blocks.zh: 每个科学家通过一个脚手架到达工作空间,这个层驱动一个统一转弯界面后面的编码代理命令行工具(§A.4). 我们的实验集中在两个脚手架上: 运行Anthropic模型的Claude Code和运行OpenAI模型的Codex. 同样的牵引装置也支持其他特工,包括双子座,基米和格罗克,因此一个单一的任务可以贯穿一系列模型. 我们优先考虑提供商的官方代理脚手架, 因为一个模型及其脚手架是一起评估的,并不是每个模型都穿过同一个脚手架,所以被比较的单位是和它的脚手架一起的模型,一个脚手架的差异是比较测量的一部分,而不是被控制的东西.

blocks.en: G.4 Models
blocks.zh: G.4 模式

blocks.en: We evaluate scientists built on models from seven providers: Anthropic ( Fable 5.1 , Fable 5 , Opus 4.8 , and Opus 4.7 ), OpenAI ( GPT 6 Astra , GPT 5.6 Sol , GPT 5.5 , and GPT 5.4 ), Zhipu ( GLM 5.2 and GLM 5.1 ), Moonshot ( Kimi K2.7 and Kimi K2.6 ), MiniMax ( MiniMax M3 and MiniMax M2.7 ), Xiaomi ( MiMo V2.5 Pro ), and DeepSeek ( DeepSeek V4 ). Anthropic and OpenAI models run through their official scaffolds; the rest run through Claude Code against an Anthropic-compatible gateway (§ G.3 ). Every model is run at the extra-high (xhigh) reasoning-effort setting, or at its highest available setting if it does not support xhigh, so models are judged at full strength rather than at a throttled setting.
blocks.zh: 我们评价来自下列七个供应商的模型为基础的科学家:Anthropic(5.1号、5号、4号、4号、4号、4号)、OpenAI(GPT 6 Astra、GPT 5.6 Sol、GPT 5.5和GPT 5.4)、Zhipu(GLM 5.2和GLM 5.1)、月光拍摄(Kimi K2.7和Kimi K2.6)、MiniMax(M3和Minimax M2.7)、小米(MiMo V2.5 Pro)和DeepSeek(DeepSeek V4)。 Anthropic和OpenAI模型通过其官方脚手架运行;其余则通过Claude Code运行,对抗一个Anthropic兼容的网关(§G.3). 每个模型都是在超高(x高)推理-努力设置下运行,或者在没有支持x高的情况下在其最高可用设置下运行,因此模型是在全强而不是在节奏设置下判断的.

blocks.en: G.5 Evaluation Trials
blocks.zh: G.5 评价审判

blocks.en: Every trial hands the scientist the same resources, so a difference in outcome reflects the model and not the budget behind it. A trial runs under a ceiling of 200 turns and a compute budget of 30 GPU-hours, with at most 2 GPUs held at once, accounted by Nexus (§ A.2 ). A trial that aborts for a transient infrastructure reason, such as a gateway timeout or a compute-pool blip, is retried up to three times before it is recorded as a failure; retries cover infrastructure, never an agent that simply solved the task poorly, so no model is re-run for doing badly. We cap in-flight trials at 30 and split that capacity evenly across the active models, so a fast API does not crowd a slower one out of the queue. Each model is run in both evaluation modes of § E.1 . GPU-hours are counted as wall-clock time times the number of GPUs held, without weighting by accelerator class, so a trial scheduled onto faster cards can fit more experimentation into the same nominal budget; we treat this as a known limitation of expressing the budget in raw GPU-hours.
blocks.zh: 每个试验都把同样的资源交给科学家,所以结果的不同反映了模型而不是背后的预算. 审判在200轮的上限下进行,计算预算为30GPU小时,最多一次举行2个GPU,由Nexus负责(第A.2节)。 以网关超时或计算池 blip等瞬间基础设施原因中止的试验,在被记录为故障之前,最多重复三次;复试覆盖基础设施,绝不是单纯解决不良任务的代理,因此没有模式因为做不好而被重新运行. 我们把飞行中的试验限制在30, 并且将这种能力平分在活跃的模型上, 所以快速的API不会挤出一个慢的排队。 每种模式都采用E.1节的两个评价模式。 GPU-hours被计算为持有GPU数的壁时倍数,不用加速器类加权,所以安排在更快的卡片上的试验可以将更多的实验配合到相同的名义预算中;我们将此视为以原始GPU-hours表示预算的已知限制.

blocks.en: G.6 Provider Failures
blocks.zh: G.6 供应商失败

blocks.en: A run spans thousands of unattended turns over hours or days, during which a model provider can rate-limit, throttle, or go down. The two settings absorb these interruptions differently, because they optimize for different things. When building an environment, the goal is to preserve work, so a run that fails resumes from the start of the current workflow iteration, reusing the saved workspace; a provider outage then costs at most the iteration in progress, not the whole reproduction. During evaluation, the goal is fairness, so a trial that fails before producing any score is discarded and restarted from a fresh workspace rather than resumed: no model is scored on a run that was continued mid-trajectory or warm-started from partial state, and every model meets the same clean-room conditions. A failure that occurs after scores are written is set aside for review rather than silently retried.
blocks.zh: 运行时间跨度为数千个无人看管的转弯时长或天长,在转弯期间,模型提供者可以进行定速,节流,或者下行. 这两个设置对这些中断的吸收方式不同,因为它们对不同的事物进行了优化. 在构建环境时,目标是保存工作,因此从当前工作流程迭代开始就无法恢复的运行,重用已保存的工作空间;供应商退出,则最多花费在进行中的迭代,而不是整个复制. 在评估期间,目标是公平,因此在产生任何分数之前失败的试运行会被丢弃,从一个新的工作空间重新开始,而不是恢复:在从部分状态继续的中导或温暖启动的跑道上没有得分的模型,每个模型都满足同样的清洁室条件. 记分后发生的失败被留待审查,而不是默默地重审.

blocks.en: G.7 Cohort and Normalization
blocks.zh: G.7 合力和正常化

blocks.en: Running every model on all 1,000 selected papers would be expensive to repeat, so the headline evaluation uses a smaller fixed cohort drawn from the lower-compute environments, chosen so that a full pass stays cheap enough to run across many models and to rerun over time. Scores are normalized against a reference set of models rather than reported in absolute terms (§ E.3 ): the per-paper normalization coefficients are computed once from that reference set and then frozen, so a newly added model is scored against the existing board without shifting the numbers already reported for other models. The reference set is the current generation of each model family; older generations are scored against that frozen reference but kept out of it.
blocks.zh: 在所有1000份选定的论文上运行每个模型都会花费很多时间重复,因此头条评价会使用从较低的计算环境抽取的更小的固定组群,选择这样,一个完整的传球保持足够便宜,可以跨过许多模型,并随着时间的推移重新运行. 参照一组模型,而不是绝对值报告(§E.3):纸质正常化系数从该参考集合中计算一次,然后被冻结,因此,新增加的模型是在不改变已经为其他模型报告的数字的情况下比照现有模型进行。 这套参考标准是每个模范家庭的当代人;老几代人与这种冷冻的参考标准相对应,但却不被采纳。

blocks.en: G.8 Reproducibility
blocks.zh: G.8 可复制性

blocks.en: Every trial starts from the same pinned container image and the same workspace template (§ C ), so the software environment and the starting state are identical across models and stay fixed as the evaluation is rerun over months. Scoring depends only on the numbers a trial records, not on wall-clock time or the hardware it ran on (§ B.2 ), so a trial can be rescored later without rerunning the agent. We retain the full record of each trial, the agent log, the final workspace, and the jobs it submitted, so any reported score can be traced back to what the agent actually did.
blocks.zh: 每一个试验都从同一个固定的容器图像和同一个工作空间模板(§C)开始,所以软件环境和起始状态在模型上是相同的,并且随着评价在数月内重新运行而固定不变. 分数只取决于审判记录的数量,而不是墙点时间或它所运行的硬件(§B.2),因此,审判可以稍后重新计分,而无需重新运行代理. 我们保留每个试验的全部记录,代理日志,最后的工作空间,以及它提交的工作,所以任何报告的分数都可以追溯到代理的实际行为.

blocks.en: Appendix H Dataset and Training Details
blocks.zh: 附录H 数据集和培训细节

blocks.en: This appendix documents the two artifacts behind § 4 : the released trace corpus (§ 4.2 ) and the scientist trained on it (§ 4.3 ). It records how the corpus is counted, how the training data and configuration are derived from it, and the held-out protocol behind Figure 15 .
blocks.zh: 本附录记载了第4节背后的两件文物:已释放的痕量体(第4.2节)和接受过相关培训的科学家(第4.3节)。 它记录了犯罪要件的计算方式、培训数据和配置是如何从中得出的,以及图15后面的搁置协议。

blocks.en: H.1 Trace Corpus
blocks.zh: H.1 追踪公司

blocks.en: Every evaluation attempt is preserved as its own git repository, one per environment, model, and run mode. The repository is the final workspace of § C with its full commit history: the system commits after every turn (§ C.4 ), so the corpus holds the development history of each attempt rather than a cleaned final state. A trace records the research idea and its revisions, the method code as it changed, and the per-experiment logs and scores, tied together by the turn-by-turn trajectory that produced them. Attempts that regress on the source method are kept alongside those that improve on it; a corpus of research being done must include the failures.
blocks.zh: 每一次评价尝试都保留为自己的git寄存器,每个环境,模型,运行模式各一个. 寄存器是第C节的最后工作空间,它有着完全的承诺历史:系统在每次转弯后都承诺(第C.4节),因此,本体保存着每次尝试的发展历史,而不是一个干净的最终状态. 一个跟踪记录了研究想法及其修改,方法代码随着改变,以及每个实验日志和分数,与产生它们的转弯轨迹联系在一起. 在源方法方面出现倒退的尝试与改进方法的尝试同时进行;正在进行的一系列研究必须包括失败。

blocks.en: The totals in § 4.2 are computed per attempt and summed. Hours of work is the scientist’s end-to-end running wall-clock time, from the first turn of a trial to its final recorded score; summed over every preserved attempt, across all models, effort tiers, and both modes, it gives the roughly 6,400 hours reported. The per-attempt averages of Table 4 come from the same records.
blocks.zh: 第4.2节中的总数按每次尝试计算和汇总。 工作小时是科学家的末端运行时钟时间,从试运行的第一回合到最后记录的分数;总结了所有保存的尝试、所有模型、工作层次和两种模式,它给出了大约6,400小时的报告。 表4的人均费用来自同样的记录。

blocks.en: H.2 Training Data
blocks.zh: H.2 培训数据

blocks.en: All training data derives from finished evaluation traces. Each example is rooted in a task specification exactly as a scientist receives it: the problem, the constraints, and the metric to move (§ C ). The ten held-out papers of § H.4 appear in no training example.
blocks.zh: 所有培训数据都来自已完成的评价。 每个例子都植根于一个任务规定,恰如科学家所接受的那样:问题、制约因素和移动的尺度(§C)。 §H.4的10份搁置文件没有出现在培训实例中。

blocks.en: The SFT set has 1,000 examples. The prompt is the task specification; the target is the attempt’s reasoning inside <think> tags followed by its final idea. Reasoning is cleaned before training: fabricated run results and job identifiers are removed, and empirical claims are reframed as conceptual, with nothing invented or added. The set combines 925 authentic completions with 75 faithful rephrasings of the strongest completions, which round the set to 1,000 without introducing new content.
blocks.zh: SFT集有1000个例子. 提示是任务规格;目标就是尝试在“思考”标记中的推理,然后是其最终想法。 在培训前清理了理由:伪造的运行结果和职务识别符被删除,经验性诉求被重新设定为概念性诉求,没有任何发明或添加. 该套装结合了925种真实的完成和75种忠实的重写最强的完成,这集装入了1000种,而没有引入新的内容.

blocks.en: The GRPO set has 1,500 already-scored ideas, rewarded by measured outcomes only: 777 examples by the held-out test score (weight 1.0), and 723 by generalization, the test score minus the train-test overfit gap (weight 0.5). Rewards are z-normalized within each paper and mode group, so an idea is reinforced or suppressed relative to the other ideas for the same task. We deliberately exclude rewards judged by an LLM: every reward in the set is a measured result.
blocks.zh: GRPO集有1500个已经得分的想法,只通过测量结果来奖励:777个实例通过搁置测试得分(重量1.0),723个实例通过概括,测试得分减去列车测试过度适应差距(重量0.5). 奖励在每张纸张和模式组内都是z-正常化的,因此一个想法相对于同一任务的其他想法会得到加强或压制. 我们故意排除由LLM判断的奖赏:每套奖赏都是有分量的结果.

blocks.en: H.3 Training Procedure
blocks.zh: H.3 培训程序

blocks.en: The base model is Qwen3-8B in its thinking variant. Both stages train a LoRA adapter of rank 32 through Tinker ( Thinking Machines Lab, 2025 ) , and the GRPO stage continues from the SFT checkpoint.
blocks.zh: 基模型在其思维变体中为Quen3-8B. 两个阶段都通过Tinker(思维机器实验室,2025年)训练一个32级的LORA适配器,GRPO阶段从SFT检查站继续.

blocks.en: Cross-entropy on the assistant message only, learning rate 10 − 4 10^{-4} , batch size 8, 3 epochs, maximum sequence length 8,192. Training NLL decreases from 2.25 to 2.16 over the three epochs.
blocks.zh: 只在助理信息上交叉切入,学习速率10−4 10×4},批量大小8,3个纪元,最大序列长度8,192. 在三个世纪中,培训NLL从2.25减少到2.16。

blocks.en: The objective is a clipped PPO loss. The SFT policy’s log-probabilities are computed with a no-gradient forward pass and used as the reference, so the clip bounds every update to a trust region around the SFT policy. Learning rate 10 − 5 10^{-5} , batch size 16, one epoch, gradient-norm clip 1.0. Training stays bounded: the completion NLL oscillates in a stable band around the SFT baseline and never diverges. This stability is not free. An earlier variant that weighted cross-entropy by the signed advantage collapsed, because tokens with negative advantage are pushed toward unboundedly low log-probability; the clipped objective with an explicit reference policy is what makes offline training on scored ideas stable.
blocks.zh: 目标是剪辑PPO损失. SFT政策的对数概率用一个不升级的前进通道计算,并用作参考,因此片段将每一个更新都限制在SFT政策周围的一个信任区域。 学习率 10 - 5 10 - 5}, 批量尺寸 16, 一个时代, 梯度-规范剪辑 1.0. 训练仍受限制:完成NLL在SFT基线周围的稳定带中振荡,从未出现偏差. 这种稳定不是自由的。 一个较早的变体,即通过签字的优势对交叉竞争进行加权,崩溃了,因为带有负优势的标志被推向无限低的对数概率;带有明确参考政策的剪切目标是使关于得分想法的离线培训稳定下来。

blocks.en: H.4 Held-Out Evaluation
blocks.zh: H.4 长期评价

blocks.en: The gym result of Figure 15 scores ideas, not the idea generator’s own coding. For each of the ten held-out papers, one idea is sampled from each of the three checkpoints, base, SFT, and GRPO, with the same prompt format, temperature 0.7, and top-p 0.8. A single fixed implementer, GPT 5.6 Sol at the xhigh effort tier, then executes every idea in innovate mode under identical conditions: the idea is injected into the briefing with the instruction to implement it faithfully and to optimize within its framing rather than invent a different approach. Only the idea’s origin varies across the thirty runs.
blocks.zh: 图15的体育成果评分创意, 对于这10份搁置的文件,从三个检查站、基地、SFT和GRPO各抽取一个想法,采用同样的即时格式,温度0.7,最高0.8。 一个单一的固定执行者,在x高强度工作级的GPT 5.6 Sol,然后在相同的条件下以创新模式执行每一个想法:该想法被注入到简报中的指示中,以忠实地执行,并在框架范围内优化,而不是发明不同的方法. 只有这个想法的起源在三十年中有所不同。

blocks.en: Scoring is identical to the benchmark: the held-out FNI, computed with each paper’s frozen cohort coefficients (§ G.7 ). The ablation is isolated from the leaderboard: it runs in a separate workspace namespace, shifts no normalization, and publishes nothing.
blocks.zh: 计分标准与基准相同:以每份文件的冻结组群系数计算出的搁置的FNI(§G.7)。 lation离头板:它运行在单独的工作空间命名空间中,转不常态,不发布任何消息.

blocks.en: Figure 38 plots each trained idea’s score against the same paper’s base idea score, and Table 14 summarizes the distributions over the ten held-out papers. Both the mean and the median rise monotonically from base to SFT to GRPO. The spread grows as well, so the gain is a shift in the typical outcome rather than a uniform improvement on every paper.
blocks.zh: 图38对照同一份论文的基本思想得分列出了每个受训思想的得分,表14总结了十份搁置论文的分布情况。 平均和中位数均由基数单调上升至SFT至GRPO. 传播范围也有所扩大,因此收益是典型结果的转变,而不是每纸上的统一改进.

blocks.en: Figure 38 : Trained ideas against the base. Each of the ten held-out papers contributes one SFT and one GRPO dot, plotted against the same paper’s base idea score (displayed scaled by 100). A dot above the dashed diagonal means the trained idea beat the untrained idea on that paper.
blocks.zh: 图38:针对基地训练思想. 这十份被搁置的论文中,每份都提供了一份SFT和一个GPRO点,根据同一份论文的基本思想得分(比分100)进行策划。 一个点在破碎的对角上 意味着训练有素的点击败了那张纸上未经训练的点子

blocks.en: Table 14 : Ablation summary statistics. Median, mean, and standard deviation of the held-out score over the ten held-out papers, displayed scaled by 100.
blocks.zh: 表14:汇总统计数据。 中度 中度 和被搁置得分的标准偏差 超过10份被搁置的论文, 显示比例为100。

blocks.en: Appendix I Example Produced Environment
blocks.zh: 附录一 生产的环境实例

blocks.en: This section uses one finished environment as a lens on what the builders actually do, and why. For each choice a builder makes while turning a paper into a reusable task, we ask why it makes that choice and whether the behavior is one the system is built to elicit or the builder’s own judgment. The paper is only background: it is the reproduction of Transformers without Normalization (arXiv:2503.10622), whose Dynamic Tanh (DyT) replaces Layer Normalization with a learnable element-wise operation. The run used MiniMax M2.7 , GLM 5.1 , and GPT 5.4 across 25 agent sessions over the reproduce, design, package, and verify roles, and about 19 GPU-hours, ending at the core_claim milestone. The few excerpts below come from the produced workspace; layout follows Figure 25 .
blocks.zh: 本节用一个完成的环境作为透镜来观察建造者的实际行为和原因. 建造者在将纸变成可重复使用的任务时, 都会做出选择, 论文只有背景:它是不规范化的变形器的复制(arXiv:2503.10622),其动态Tanh(DyT)用可学习元素的操作取代层规范化. 运行使用MiniMax M2.7,GLM 5.1,和GPT 5.4跨25个代理会话,围绕复制,设计,包装,和验证角色,以及约19个GPU小时,以核心-索赔里程碑结束. 以下几个节选来自生产的工作空间;布局遵循图25.

blocks.en: The reproducer writes the paper’s actual computation rather than a model tuned to emit its published numbers. It does this because the milestone rewards a method that runs: a surrogate fit to the reported accuracy would clear a naive number-matching test but fails ours by construction, and the verifier re-checks that the code is the algorithm itself. This is designed in — the milestone ladder and the verify role reward a runnable method (§ A.3 ).
blocks.zh: 转载者写下论文的实际计算, 它这样做是因为里程碑奖励了一种运行的方法: 符合所报告精确度的代词会清除一个天真的数字比对测试,但通过构建失败了我们的,而验证者重新检查代码是算法本身. 这是在——里程碑式阶梯和核查作用奖励一种可运行的方法(§A.3)中设计的.

LayerNorm , nn . RMSNorm )): # swap every norm layer set_submodule ( model , name , DyT ( m . normalized_shape [-1], init_alpha )) return model

blocks.en: The builder states the problem in method-agnostic terms: it fixes the question and the success criteria but never names DyT or normalization-free training. Why withhold what it just implemented? Because the same workspace is later handed to a from-scratch scientist, and a brief that named the solution would let that scientist copy it instead of doing research. By design, briefings must be method-agnostic, and the verifier and validate.py flag leaks; one is caught below.
blocks.zh: 建设者用方法不可知的术语来说明问题:它固定问题和成功标准,但从未命名DyT或无正常化训练. 为什么拒绝它刚刚执行的内容? 因为同样的工作空间后来被交给了一位来自切片的科学家, 一个给解决方案命名的简介会让这位科学家复制它而不是做研究. 从设计上讲,简报必须是方法不可知的,以及核查和验证的。 皮旗漏泄;下夹一.

blocks.en: ⬇ ## Research Question Can deep transformer - style classifiers be trained stably and accurately when their usual feature - normalization components are removed or replaced , without winning by increasing model size , changing the data , or using pretrained weights ? ## Success Criteria - Train without numerical divergence ; match or improve the reference accuracy . - Keep parameter count and model scale matched within the comparison . - Same data split and preprocessing ; no pretrained weights , extra data , or ensembles .
blocks.zh: ⬇ □ 研究问题 深层变压器 - 样式分类器在通常的特性 - 正常化组件被删除或替换时,能否被严格和准确地培训,而不通过增加模型大小、改变数据或使用预先训练的重量来赢得胜利? □ □ □ □ 成功标准 - 没有数值差异的列; 匹配或提高参考精度 。 - 在比较中保持参数计数和模型比例匹配 。 - 数据分割和预处理相同; 没有预先调整的权重、 额外数据或组合 。

blocks.en: The scoring contract is where the builder exercises judgment the system asks for but does not dictate. It makes top-1 accuracy the primary metric, keeps top-5 and balanced accuracy as diagnostics, and gives parameter count a negative coefficient — so beating the baseline by scaling the model up does not register as a win. The format invites such a constraint metric; which metrics matter, and by how much, is the builder’s call. It records the paper’s reported numbers as the ranking reference and its own measured numbers as the baseline a future method must beat.
blocks.zh: 评分合同是建筑商对系统要求的但不要求的进行判断的地方。 它使顶-1精度成为初级度量,保持顶-5和平衡的精度作为诊断,并给参数计数一个负系数——因此通过放大模型来击败基线并不能被记录为胜负. 这种格式要求这种制约性衡量标准;哪个衡量标准很重要,从多大程度上讲,建设者的呼唤才是。 它将报出的数字作为排名参考,并将自己的计量数字作为未来方法必须打破的基准。

blocks.en: The full paper trains ViT-B/L for 300 epochs, beyond a per-paper budget, so the builder scales to a 50-class slice and a ViT-S/16. The choice is bounded by a rule the system cares about: model and data scale may shrink, but the algorithm and the matched comparison must be preserved, and the task must stay hard enough to discriminate. The builder checks this — the LayerNorm baseline lands below saturation, so comparison still has room, and DyT edges it at equal parameter count.
blocks.zh: 整纸列车为300个纪元的Vit-B/L列车,超出每纸预算,因此建造者比例为50级切片和Vit-S/16. 选择以系统所关心的规则为界限:模型和数据尺度可能缩小,但必须保留算法和匹配的比较,任务必须保持足够硬度才能区分. 建造者检查了这一点——饱和度以下的LayerNorm基线土地,因此比较仍然有空间,DyT以等参数计时将其边缘.

blocks.en: Because the environment is graded by comparison, the builder writes down what a future scientist may optimize, what it must hold fixed, and where it may explore. It splits this into three documents: a target (what improvement means and how it is measured), constraints (what must stay matched across compared systems), and a direction (the mechanism to work on, and what is out of bounds). These are required and method-safe: a from-scratch reader sees the rules, not the solution.
blocks.zh: 因为环境是通过比较来分级的,建造者写下未来的科学家可以优化什么,它必须固定什么,它可以探索哪里. 它将这一点分为三个文件:目标(改进意味着什么以及衡量方法)、制约因素(在比较的系统之间必须保持匹配)和方向(工作机制以及超出范围的内容)。 这些都是需要的,方法上的安全:一个来自scratch的读者看到了规则,而不是解决方案.

blocks.en: ⬇ ## Primary : supervised_classification Improve accuracy on the matched ImageNet class slice without increasing model scale or changing the data . - Benefit : top1_accuracy ( top5_accuracy , balanced_accuracy as diagnostics ) - Constraint : param_count_M within 5% of the matched reference - Success : top -1 within 1 pt of the reference , with no parameter increase
blocks.zh: ⬇ □小学:受监督的_分类 在匹配的ImageNet类切片上提高精度,而不增加模型尺度或更改数据. - 效益:上1_准确度(上5_准确度,平衡_准确度作为诊断) - 约束:param_count_ 在匹配的参考文献的5%以内 M - 成功: 在参考文献的1 pt 内上 - 1, 没有参数增加

blocks.en: ⬇ ## Model Scale Candidate and reference must have matched scale : param_count_M within 5%. A larger candidate is an extra experiment , not an improvement . ## Training Budget Same data , epoch budget , optimizer , augmentation , and preprocessing . A recipe change counts only when it is applied to every system in the comparison .
blocks.zh: ⬇ □ 模型缩放候选人和引用必须具有匹配的缩放 : param_ counter_ M在5%之内。 一个更大的候选人是一个额外的实验,而不是改进。 □训练预算相同数据,划时代预算,优化器,扩容,预处理. 食谱改变只有在比较中适用于每个系统时才算数。

blocks.en: ⬇ ## Direction Scope Work on normalization as a mechanism : stabilize activations , gradients , or optimization while keeping the compared architecture and data fixed . ## Out of Bounds - Resource scaling as the only change - Pretrained weights or extra data - Ensembles - Switching to an easier or different dataset
blocks.zh: *□方向范围作为机制的正常化工作:稳定激活、梯度或优化,同时保持比较结构和数据的固定。 □ □ □ □ Out of Bunds - 资源缩放作为唯一的变化 - Pretrained 权重或额外数据 - Ensembles - 切换到更简单或不同的数据集

blocks.en: The builder makes the evaluator score prediction files and own the labels, rather than load the reproduced model. Why give up the convenience of calling its own checkpoint? Because a future method, however different from DyT, must score through the same interface; an evaluator coupled to this run’s model would break for everyone else. The boundary is designed — and, as the next step shows, enforced rather than assumed.
blocks.zh: 构建者制作评价者预言文件并拥有标签,而不是加载复制的模型. 为何放弃拨打自己的检查站的方便? 因为未来的方法,无论与DyT不同,都必须通过同一界面得分;一个评估员与这个运行模式相结合,就会让其他人崩溃。 边界是设计出来的,正如下一步所示,是执行而不是假定。

blocks.en: The designer adds a hidden test slice so a later scientist cannot quietly overfit the visible scores, and — notably — writes down why it chose this split and where it falls short. The choice of split is the builder’s own judgment; that it records the trade-off is the behavior the design-notes step is meant to produce.
blocks.zh: 设计者增加了一个隐藏的测试切片,这样后期的科学家就不能悄悄地过度匹配可见的分数,并且——特别是——写下它为什么选择这个分数和它落差的地方. 分拆的选择是建造者自己的判断;它记录权衡是设计笔记步骤意在产生的行为.

blocks.en: ⬇ ### Split style : per - class alternating validation parity Within each class , even - position images go to train and odd - position to test . Why this fits : both slices have comparable difficulty , so an honest method scores similarly on both , while a method that games the visible slice shows a gap . Known limitation : the parity split is moderate . A harder split ( held - out classes or OOD ) gives a stronger shortcut signal but needs a larger dataset .
blocks.zh: QQ 分割样式: 每类交替验证等价 在每一类,甚至 - 位置图像去训练 和奇怪的位置 - 测试。 为什么这符合 : 两个切片都有相似的难度, 所以诚实的方法在两个上都得分相似, 而游戏可见切片的方法则显示一个缺口 。 已知限制 : 平分为中等 。 更硬的分割( 持有 - 退出类或 OOD ) , 提供了更强大的快捷键信号, 但需要更大的数据集 。

blocks.en: The last role is where design meets behavior. The verifier audited the artifact and found that an earlier builder had let the evaluator load the reproduced checkpoint — a method leak that would silently break from-scratch mode. It moved inference into method/ and rewrote eval/ as a generic prediction-file scorer. The system is built to catch exactly this class of error (the verify role together with validate.py ), and here it did.
blocks.zh: 最后一个角色是设计与行为相遇的地方. 核查员对文物进行了审计,发现一个较早的建造者让评估员加载了复制的检查站——这种方法的泄露会静悄悄地打破切换模式. 它将推论推向方法/并重写 eval/作为通用的预测文件计分器. 系统是用来准确捕捉这一类错误的(验证角色与验证.py),在这里它做到了.

blocks.en: ⬇ ## Issues found - Critical , fixed : eval / contained solution - specific checkpoint loading . Even without importing from method /, this leaked the reproduced algorithm into the reusable evaluation path and would compromise from - scratch mode . ## Fixes applied - Moved checkpoint inference into method /; rewrote eval / as a generic evaluator that scores JSONL predictions from any method without knowing the algorithm .
blocks.zh: ⬇ □ 发现的问题 -- -- 危急问题、固定问题: eval / 包含溶液 -- -- 具体的检查站装载问题。 即便不从方法 / 导入, 这也会将复制的算法泄露到可重复使用的评价路径中, 并且会从 - 抓取模式 中妥协 。 □ □ □ □ fixs 应用 - 将检查站推论移到方法 /;rerote eval / 作为通用评价员,在不知晓算法的情况下从任何方法中评分JSONL的预测.

blocks.en: Only after this check passed did the workspace settle at core_claim . Every choice above is committed: the run writes a manifest.json and a README.md reproduction log, and the git history checkpoints each turn, so each decision traces back to the builder, the jobs, and the code behind it (§ C ).
blocks.zh: 只有在通过此检查后, 工作空间才算为 Core_ claim 。 上面的每个选择都是承诺的:跑步者会写一个清单。 Json和一个读物。 md复制日志和git历史检查站各转弯,所以每个决定都追溯到建筑商,工作,以及后面的代码(§C).

blocks.en: Appendix J Agent Prompts
blocks.zh: 附录 J 代理提示

blocks.en: This section shows representative prompts from each stage of the system, to illustrate how agents are instructed: the screening and analysis prompts that grade and select papers, the role prompts that drive a Swarm reproduction, and the prompts that run a single evaluation trial. The prompts are excerpted; operational scaffolding repeated across prompts (job submission, progress logging, version control, the workspace layout) is omitted and described in sections above. Placeholders in braces are filled at run time.
blocks.zh: 本节显示系统各个阶段的代表性提示,以说明代理人如何被指示:筛选和分析提示该等级和选择论文,角色提示驱动Swarm复制,以及运行单一评价试验的提示. 提示被摘录;操作脚手架重复跨提示(工作提交,进度记录,版本控制,工作空间布局)被省略,并在以上章节中描述. 架子上的占位符在运行时填充.

blocks.en: J.1 Prompts for Paper Grading and Selection
blocks.zh: J.1 纸张分级和选择提示

blocks.en:
Prefilter Paper Pre-Filter Read the paper excerpt below and rate its research quality on a scale of 0-100. • 100 : Landmark paper. Defines a new field or sets a new paradigm. Must-read for anyone in ML/AI. • 80 : Top-venue quality (ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, ACL, EMNLP, CVPR). Novel idea, strong experiments, clear results. Worth reading and citing. • 60 : Second-tier venue quality. Solid work with experiments, but less novelty or narrower scope. Worth reading in your area. • 40 : Has a method and some experiments, but limited novelty or weak evaluation. You’d skim it. • 20 : Minimal contribution. Shallow, incremental, or poorly executed. Not worth reading. • 0 : Not a research paper, or no method and no experiments. These anchors are reference points, not buckets. Use the full range freely.
Scores like 7, 23, 41, 58, 73, 84, and 97 are all valid when appropriate.
Do not restrict yourself to only 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, or 100. Note: The excerpt below is the first ~15,000 characters of the paper, converted to markdown, intentionally truncated. Formatting artifacts (broken text, missing figures, odd symbols) are from automatic PDF-to-markdown conversion — ignore them and judge only the research content. Think briefly about the paper’s contribution, novelty, and experimental rigor.
Give a short explanation of the main strengths and weaknesses.
Then provide an overall score from 0 to 100, using any integer in that range.
The score should reflect the paper’s actual research quality, not just which
anchor it is closest to. Paper Excerpt
blocks.zh:
预过滤纸预过滤器 阅读下面的论文节录,并将其研究质量评定为0-100级. • 100:地标纸。 定义新字段或设置新范式。 任何在ML/AI的人必须阅读。 • 80:最高服务质量(ICLR、NeurIPS、ICML、ACL、EMNLP、CVPR)。 小说思想,强力实验,结果清晰. 值得阅读和引用。 • 60:二级会场质量。 与实验的扎实工作,但不太新奇或范围较窄. 值得在你的区域阅读。 • 40:有方法和一些实验,但新颖性有限或评价薄弱。 你省省吧。 • 20:最小贡献。 浅薄 递增 或执行不力 不值得阅读。 • 0:不是研究论文,或没有方法和实验。 这些锚是参考点,不是水桶. 全程自由使用.
得分如7,23,41,58,73,84,97等均在适当时有效.
不要把自己限制在 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 或100。 说明: 下面的节选是纸的第一个~15,000个字符,转换为标记下,故意截断. 格式化的文物(破碎的文字,缺失的数字,奇数符号)来自自动PDF到标记的转换——忽略它们,只判断研究内容. 简略考虑一下论文的贡献、新颖性和实验性。
简要说明主要优缺点.
然后提供从0到100的总分,使用该范围内的任何整数.
得分应该反映论文的实际研究质量,而不是仅仅反映论文的实际研究质量。
锁定它最接近。 纸张摘录

blocks.en: Analyst PaperScope — Paper Cataloging Prompt You are a research paper analyst. Given a paper, produce a structured catalog entry of 13 fields whose purpose is to assess whether and how hard the paper can be reproduced. The fields cover paper type, novelty, taxonomy, compute requirements, paid resources, benchmarks, datasets, baselines, dependencies, code availability, reproduction difficulty, paper quality, and problem novelty. Every score is an integer on a 0–10 scale, grounded in specific paper content; when uncertain, say so rather than guess. Field 1: Paper Type Classify into one primary type, with justification: • metric_method — introduces or improves a method, evaluated with measurable results. • benchmark_dataset — the contribution is a benchmark, dataset, or evaluation suite. • analysis_findings — an empirical discovery or insight rather than an improvement. • theoretical — a formal result: proofs, bounds, complexity analysis. • survey_position — aggregates or opines on existing work; no original experiments. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] Scoring: Reproduction Difficulty, Paper Quality, Problem Novelty The decisive fields. Reproduction difficulty — split into coding, compute, runtime, and data sub-scores plus an overall — estimates the cost to implement the method, run it, and evaluate the main claims, judged as the AI agent that would reproduce it rather than a human. Paper quality rates the contribution as a reviewer would. Problem novelty rates how interesting the question is, independent of the method. Each is a 0–10 integer with a short justification. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,]
blocks.zh: 分析纸张范围——纸张编目提示 你是一个研究论文分析师。 根据一份文件,编制一个有条理的目录条目,由13个字段组成,其目的是评估该文件是否可以复制以及复制的难度。 字段涵盖纸张类型,新颖性,分类学,计算要求,付费资源,基准,数据集,基线,依赖性,代码可用性,复制难度,纸张质量,以及问题新颖性. 每个分数都是0–10尺度的整数,以具体的纸面内容为基础;当不确定时,就这么说而不是猜测. 第1栏:纸张类型分类为一种主要类型,说明理由: • 度量法——采用或改进一种方法,并作出可衡量的评价。 • 基准-数据集——贡献是基准、数据集或评价套件。 • 分析-调查——经验性发现或见解,而不是改进。 • 理论——一种正式的结果:证据、界限、复杂性分析。 • 调查-位置——对现有工作的汇总或看法;无原始实验。 [ \,\ cdots\,] 分类:复制难度,纸张质量,问题小说 决定性的领域。 复制难度——分为编码,计算,运行时间,和数据子分数加总分——估算实施方法的成本,运行,评价主要索赔,判断为将复制方法的AI代理而不是人类. 作为审查者,纸张质量评定贡献。 问题的新颖性评价了这个问题有多有趣,独立于方法. 每个是0-10整数,并有简短的理由。 [⋯,\,]

blocks.en: J.2 Prompts for Swarm
blocks.zh: J.2 冲锋枪的提示

blocks.en: Reproduce Start Reproducer Agent You are a Reproducer agent. Your job is to read a research paper, reproduce its core results, and package the reproduction as a reusable environment. Your reproduction does not need to match the paper’s exact numbers, but you must implement the paper’s actual method and demonstrate that it works as claimed. Fitting surrogates to published data, hardcoding paper values, or building shortcuts that bypass the method are not reproduction — they are fabrication. You are fully autonomous. There is no human in the loop. Do not ask for confirmation, do not wait for direction, do not say "let me know" or "please confirm". Analyze the situation, make your own decisions, and act immediately. Every turn you spend not making concrete progress (editing code, creating scripts, fixing bugs) is wasted. You should launch multi- or sub-agents to accelerate the implementation. Your minimum goal is core_claim . Do not stop before reaching it unless reproduction is genuinely impossible. You may receive a newly initialized workspace, or one that already has partial or substantial implementations. In either case, your job is to push the reproduction forward — not just audit what exists. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] Workflow Work through these phases. You decide when to move between them — they are not hard boundaries. Phase A: Paper Analysis (no GPU needed) 1. Read the paper thoroughly (both markdown and PDF) 2. Identify: dataset, method, evaluation metric, baseline numbers, hyperparameters 3. Check if the paper links to a code repository 4. Check if the paper has a code release — if so, clone it into method/ and study it 5. Plan your implementation — whether building on existing code or writing from scratch, the paper’s method goes in method/ 6. Write an initial plan as comments or a brief README 7. Fill in the briefing/ folder — problem.md and evaluation.md first (method-agnostic), then method.md , and finally overview.md (short summary) 8. Fill in scoring/reference.json with the paper’s reported numbers — experiments, metrics, baselines, and the proposed method (see Deliverables for format) Phase B: Environment Setup (light compute) 1. Acquire the dataset: check the shared datasets directory first, download if missing (use shared for general datasets, workspace data/ for paper-specific ones) 2. Download pretrained models if needed (use shared models directory for general weights, workspace for paper-specific ones) 3. Write data loading and preprocessing code 4. Write the evaluation script (compute the paper’s metric) 5. Validate scoring/reference.json by running python validate.py 6. Verify on a trivial baseline (e.g., random predictions) that the eval pipeline works 7. Start drafting the container definition and task description for the environment Phase C: Reproduction (GPU, iterative) Plan the reproduction incrementally — start from the minimum, expand if budget allows: 1. Plan first. Break the reproduction into ordered steps from minimum to complete. 2. Reproduce the minimum that supports the core claim. A single experiment on one setting — just enough to show the method works. 3. Expand incrementally. Each step adds more coverage — more settings, more comparisons, more of the paper’s results. But only expand after the minimum is confirmed working — validating that the idea works matters far more than matching the paper’s full scale. 4. Mark progress. Report milestones (see below) after each turn. When expanding, prefer adding a new axis of variation over running more of the same single-setting experiment. The relevant axes depend on the paper: dataset, problem instance, input difficulty, environment, backbone, hyperparameter regime, task type — anything the paper itself varies. A small matrix across two axes is far more informative than two runs at the same condition, and it gives downstream agents a real surface to improve on. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,]
blocks.zh: 复制开始复制代理 你是一个复制商代理。 你的工作是阅读研究论文,复制其核心成果,并将复制包装成可重复使用的环境. 您的复制不需要与纸张的准确数字相匹配, 但你必须执行纸张的实际方法, 并证明它能像所声称的那样工作。 将替代物装配到已公布的数据,硬编码纸值,或者建造绕过方法的快捷键都不是复制——它们是捏造的. 你是完全自主的。 圈子里没有人类 不要要求确认,不要等待方向,不要说"让我知道"或"请确认". 分析情况 自己做决定 立刻行动 您花费的每个转弯没有取得具体进展(编辑代码、创建脚本、修复错误)都被浪费了。 应当推出多剂或副剂以加速实施. 你的最低进球是核心目标 在到达之前不要停下来,除非真的不可能复制。 您可获得新初始化的工作空间,或已经部分或全部实施的工作空间。 无论哪种情况,你的工作是推动复制工作向前发展,而不仅仅是审计现有的情况。 [\,\cdots\] 工作流程工作贯穿这些阶段。 你决定何时在它们之间移动——它们不是硬边界。 A阶段:纸张分析(不需要GPU) 1. 彻底阅读文件(降标和PDF) 2. 确定:数据集、方法、评价尺度、基准数、超参数 3. 检查纸张是否链接到代码存储库 4. 检查纸张是否有代码释放——如果有的话,将其复制成方法/研究5. 规划你的实施——无论是在现有守则的基础上还是从零开始写,文件的方法都采用方法/ 6. 将初步计划写成评论或简短的7号读物。 填写简报/文件夹-问题.md和评价。 md先(方法-不可知论),然后是方法.md,最后是概述. md(简要) 8. 填上评分/参考.json, 填上论文报告的数字 -- -- 实验、衡量标准、基线和拟议方法(格式见交付品) B阶段:环境设置(轻计算) 1. 获取数据集:先检查共享数据集目录,缺失时下载(通用数据集共享,工作空间数据/纸张专用数据共享). 2. 必要时下载预先培训过的模型(使用通用权重的共享模型目录,特定纸张的工作空间) 3. 写入数据加载和预处理代码 4. 撰写评审脚本(计算论文的度量) 5. 通过运行python验证.py验证积分/参考.json 6. 对微小的基线(例如随机预测)进行核实,以确定输油管工程 7. 开始起草环境阶段C的容器定义和任务说明:复制(GPU,迭代) 计划逐步复制——从最低限度开始,在预算允许的情况下扩大: 1. 先计划。 复制从最小到完成 2. 重新提出支持核心索赔的最低数额。 在一个设定上进行单一的实验——仅仅足以显示方法的作用. 3. 逐步扩大。 每一步都增加了更多的覆盖面——更多的设置,更多的比较,更多的论文结果. 但只有在最低限被确认有效后才能扩大——验证这个想法的效用远比论文的全面规模重要得多. 4. 标出进展。 在每个回合之后报告里程碑(见下文)。 在扩展时,宁可添加一个新的变异轴,也不愿运行更多相同的单设实验. 相关的轴取决于纸张:数据集,问题实例,输入难度,环境,骨干,超参数系统,任务类型——任何纸张本身都不同. 横跨两轴的小矩阵在相同条件下比两条运行要多得多,它使下游的物剂有了真正的表面来改进. blocks.en: On Designer Designer — Build the Train/Test Evaluation You are the designer . Previous agents reproduced a paper and produced scoring/scores.json . Your job is to design a two-part evaluation — a train slice and a held-out test slice — that future agents will be tested against. You might be resuming from a previous designer’s work, or a repo not yet started on this part. Training and test should be roughly equal in scale. What this workspace is becoming This workspace will ship as a reusable benchmark and gym environment . Future AI scientist agents will operate on it in two modes: • Improve mode : the agent gets everything (problem + method + code + results + data + documentation) and must beat the current scores . • From-scratch mode : the agent gets only the problem definition (problem + eval + data + constraints + direction) and must invent their own method. In both modes, the agent optimizes against an evaluation suite (what in eval/ ). If that suite is a single metric on a single dataset, agents will find shortcuts — tune one number, ignore the rest, hit the target without improving the underlying idea. We want to measure real improvement, not metric-hacking. Your job is to make that harder (or at least detectable) by creating two evaluation slices: • eval/train/ — the slice future agents see during development. They optimize against this. • eval/test/ — held out from future agents. They never see it. When they signal "done", we run eval/test/ on their final method. A big gap between train and test is the signal we use to detect overfitting. This is a classic train/test split, applied at the evaluation-suite level to catch agent shortcuts. You are evaluating future agents’ work, not the paper’s claim. You are not trying to break the paper. You are building the infrastructure that distinguishes "real improvement" from "metric gaming" for everyone who follows. What to produce Six new files / directories total — two new eval subfolders, two new score files, two new shell entry-points (existing files are read-only, except reference.json , which you may extend with new metric entries only): ⬇ eval / |-- < existing eval files DO NOT MODIFY > |-- train / <- new , self - contained , what future agents see ‘-- test / <- new , self - contained , held out from future agents scoring / |-- reference . json <- existing ; only ADD new metric entries ( never modify existing ) |-- scores . json <- existing , DO NOT MODIFY |-- scores_train . json <- new , produced by scripts / evaluate_train . sh ‘-- scores_test . json <- new , produced by scripts / evaluate_test . sh scripts / |-- evaluate . sh <- existing , DO NOT MODIFY |-- evaluate_train . sh <- new , mirrors evaluate . sh ’ s contract ‘-- evaluate_test . sh <- new , mirrors evaluate . sh ’ s contract THESE SCORES MUST BE PRODUCED BY A REAL RUN. YOU CANNOT GUESS OR HARDCODE ANY NUMBERS IN THEM. Format follows the existing scoring/scores.json and scoring/reference.json conventions. Each metric entry should have at least a value: field. If reference.json uses coefficient to weight metrics, carry those coefficients into both new files consistently so the aggregates are comparable. Plus two new shell entry-points alongside the existing scripts/evaluate.sh (do NOT modify evaluate.sh ): • scripts/evaluate_train.sh — runs eval/train/ on a method’s pre-generated outputs and writes scoring/scores_train.json • scripts/evaluate_test.sh — runs eval/test/ on the same outputs and writes scoring/scores_test.json These follow the same contract as the existing scripts/evaluate.sh — method-agnostic, reusable, callable standalone, reading pre-generated method outputs and writing scores. Mirror evaluate.sh ’s argument shape and input/output conventions exactly — a future agent should be able to swap in a different method and run scripts/evaluate_train.sh / scripts/evaluate_test.sh without code changes on their side. evaluate_test.sh must score every method present in scores_train.json (never one hardcoded name), write to scores_test.json , and invoke the eval/test/ path. A copy of evaluate_train.sh that still points at eval/train/ silently destroys the anti-shortcut signal. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] Design principles Metrics measure the scientific quantity, NEVER agreement with the paper This is the single most important rule. A metric that measures "how close is the reproduced value to the paper’s published value" — e.g., mean_abs_rel_error_author_X , deviation_from_paper_X , |value - 0.87| , fit_to_published_Y — is categorically forbidden as a scored metric. The gym is built FROM the paper, but we are never trying to match the paper. The paper is context , not a target. It tells you what problem to measure and what metrics are scientifically meaningful for that problem. It does NOT tell you what numbers the score should reach. Future agents may produce a method that scores higher than the paper (real improvement), lower than the paper (regression), or that invents an entirely different approach — every one of those outcomes must be visible in the score. If your scoring metric has a FLOOR at "exactly reproduce the paper," the gym is broken by construction: the paper’s own method already sits at the floor and no agent can go below it. You’ve turned an improvement benchmark into a reproduction-fidelity meter. What TO score: • The scientific quantity itself (accuracy, loss, F1, calibration error, similarity, detection rate, reward, etc.), computed on the paper’s evaluation protocol. Avoid wall-clock-dependent quantities such as latency or runtime; use a machine-independent substitute (FLOPs, parameter count, training steps, samples processed) instead, since the verifier rejects scored wall-clock-speed metrics. • Continuous metrics whose range spans both directions of the paper’s claim — an agent that beats the paper’s reported X=0.87 with X=0.95 must score higher; an agent that scores X=0.80 must score lower. • Ratios, directional differences, or any quantity where "the paper’s number" is simply one point on a continuum that future methods can move along. What NOT to score: • |reproduced - paper_published| (absolute error vs paper) • mean_abs_rel_error_author_* or any metric whose name includes author , paper , published , vs_paper , deviation_from_paper , reproduction_error , or equivalent wording. • Any metric whose theoretical floor equals "the paper’s published value." If matching the paper gives 0 and lower-is-better, you have built the forbidden thing — even if the metric name hides it. The paper’s numbers belong in scoring/reference.json under results.<method_name> as the baseline against which future agents are ranked. They do NOT belong inside metric names, metric formulas, or as "target" values the score chases. Anti-shortcut, not anti-paper A well-reproduced method should score similarly on train and test . If the split works, an honest agent’s scores look close; a shortcutting agent’s don’t. Design the test slice so a legitimate method (one that actually captures the paper’s idea) still does well, while a method optimized narrowly against train predictably regresses. Do not hardcode which method to evaluate. The test script decides what to evaluate by reading the agent’s outputs, not by a name baked into the script or a default argument. If your evaluator only evaluates one name, a future agent’s improvements will never reach it and every improve-mode run looks identical on test — silently. Train and test must be calibrated to comparable difficulty The split only works if train and test probe the method at roughly the same level of rigor . If test is drastically harder than train by construction, every method will score worse on test — that gap comes from your design, not from overfitting, and it tells you nothing. If test is drastically easier, everyone ceilings out and there’s nothing to compare. The calibration target: on the existing final reproduction , train and test should produce scores that are meaningfully comparable side-by-side. A small, expected gap is fine; a huge collapse means your split is miscalibrated, not that the reproduction is bad. When using a split style that intrinsically shifts difficulty (difficulty stratification, OOD/perturbed, held-out subgroup), keep the shift moderate — enough to surface methods that don’t generalize, not so much that even a legitimate method breaks. Sanity-check by running the existing final checkpoint on both slices before you declare the split final: if train scores are strong and test scores collapse, back off and re-design. Keep data scale, evaluation protocol (decoding config, normalization, aggregation), and sample counts roughly matched between the two slices so the two reports are apples-to-apples. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] Self-contained (critical) Core idea: once a future agent has optimized against eval/train/ and signaled done, running eval/test/ on their method must be a zero-effort step. No retraining. No re-running expensive experiments. No code changes on the agent’s side. Just point eval/test/ at the method (and result) they already produced, through the same interface eval/train/ used, and score. As if we got a score by running the train set. evaluate_test.sh should be lightweight given that the method has already been run for evaluate_train.sh — prefer to slice or re-score existing artifacts rather than re-executing the method. If you do need to call the method again (e.g. for a stochastic-seed split), make sure the extra cost is small. This means eval/test/ has to go through the same pre-agreed method interface that eval/train/ uses — the contract that already exists here between method/ and eval/ (a function signature, a CLI like scripts/method.sh , a predictions file at a fixed path, etc.). The agent writes their method to satisfy that interface using eval/train/ as the visible spec. eval/test/ then calls the same interface and scores — nothing else required from the agent. If eval/test/ couples to anything specific to the current method/ (an internal class, a particular checkpoint format, a file that only this training run happens to write), a future different method won’t satisfy it — and the test breaks through no fault of the agent. The set of keys under experiments.<exp>.results (or the equivalent method-name axis) must match between scores_train.json and scores_test.json . When an agent adds a new method variant on train, the test script must automatically score it on test — not by re-running evaluate_test.sh with a different name, but because the script discovers and iterates over whatever methods it finds. The method-name contract is enforced by the script’s enumeration logic, not by a caller remembering to pass the right argument. No leakage between train and test eval/train/ and eval/test/ must be independent . eval/train/ must not import from eval/test/ , and vice versa. Do not put shared helpers inside either folder that the other reads — if you need shared code, duplicate it (the two folders are small) or keep it outside both. A future agent reading eval/train/ to optimize must not be able to learn the test set’s metrics, data split, or scoring details by following an import. scoring/reference.json is fine — it may document both slices; that’s expected. Top-level eval/ files (outside train/ and test/ ) should preferably not reveal test-specific metric/data shape either — if you can avoid it, do. Do NOT retrain. Do NOT modify the method. The method is already built by prior agents. You are only re-running inference + scoring on the existing final checkpoint. If there is no usable checkpoint or scoring/scores.json is missing, run the minimal inference path to produce scores — but do not retrain, change hyperparameters, or tweak the method. You are encouraged to use as little computing resource as possible. In most cases, you do not need to rerun massive experiments. For example, the previous result might be already saved, and you only need to re-evaluate some rubric-based scores or the model is already trained, and you only need to do some lightweight evaluation. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,]
blocks.zh: 关于设计师——建设列车/测试评价 你是设计师。 前任特工复制了一份文件,并制作了评分/分数.json。 你的工作是设计一个分两部分的评估——一个列车切片和一个搁置的测试切片——来测试未来的特工. 您可能要恢复先前设计师的作品, 或尚未开始的回购 。 培训和测试的规模应大致相等。 这个工作空间正在变成什么 这个工作空间将作为一个可重复使用的基准和健身环境。 未来的AI科学家代理将在它上操作两种模式: • 改进模式:代理获得一切(问题+方法+代码+结果+数据+文档),必须击败当前分数. ^ From-scratch模式:代理只获得问题定义(问题+eval+数据+约束+方向),必须发明自己的方法. 在两种模式中,代理都比照一个评价套件(什么在eval/)进行优化. 如果该套套件是单一数据集上的单个度量,代理商会找到快捷键——调一号,忽略其余,击中目标而不改进基本想法. 我们想衡量真正的改进,而不是衡量打击。 你的工作是创造两个评价片块,使这个更难(或至少可以探测): eval/train/——开发过程中看到的未来的切片剂. 他们优化了这一点。 • eval/测试/——来自未来代理人。 他们从来没有看到它。 当它们发出“done”信号时, 我们运行 eval/测试/ 在他们的最终方法。 列车和测试之间的巨大差距就是我们用来检测超合的信号. 这是一种经典的列车/测试拆分,在评价-套用级别上应用来捕捉代理快捷键. 您正在评估未来代理人的工作,而不是报社的索赔。 你没有试图打破报纸。 你们正在建设基础设施, 将“真正的改善”和“量子游戏”区别开来, 怎样生产六个新的文件/目录总计——两个新的eval子文件夹,两个新的分数文件,两个新的 shell 条目点(现有的文件是只读的,除了引用. json,您仅可添加新的参数条目: eval / |- < 现有 eval文件 DO NOT MODIFY > – train / <- new, self - 包含,未来代理所看到的 '- 测试 / <- new, self - 包含,来自未来代理商的评分 / |-参考. json < 现有;只有 ADD 新的度量衡条目(从未修改过现有) – 分数 . json < – 现有, DO NOT MODIFY < – 分数_train. json < – new,由脚本制作/评价_train. sh '-分数_测试. json < 新的,由脚本制作/评价_测试. sh脚本 / |-评价. sh <- 现有,DO NOT MODIFY –-评价_ train. sh < - new, sh < 镜像评价. SH 合同 : " - 评估 - 测试. sh < - 新的,镜像评估。 sh ' serres的合同必须由真正的跑步生产。 你不能猜 或硬码 任何数字在这些。 格式遵循现有的积分/分数.json和积分/参考.json常规. 每个参数条目至少应有一个值:字段。 若参考. json对权重度量使用系数,将这些系数一致地带入两个新文件,因此总量是可比的。 加上两个与现有脚本/评价.sh(不修改评价.sh):脚本/评价_train.sh——在方法预生成的输出上运行eval/train/,并写出评分/scores_train.json •脚本/评价_test.sh——在同一输出上运行eval/test/,并写出评分/score_test.json 这些与现有的脚本/评价.sh——方法不可知,可重复使用,可调用的独立,读取预先生成的方法输出和写分数的相同合同. Mirror 评估.sh 的参数形状和输入/输出常规——未来的代理商应该能够以不同的方法互换,运行脚本/评价_train.sh /脚本/评价_test.sh而不在他们一方更改代码. val/ test/路径。 评估_train.sh的复制品,仍然指向eval/train/无声破坏反短发信号. [\,\cdots\] [\,\cdots\] 设计原理测量科学数量, 从来没有同意论文 这是唯一的最重要的规则。 一个衡量“复制值与报纸的出版值有多接近”的度量标准——例如:eal_abs_rel_error_author__X,偏差_paper__X,QQ值−0.87|,fit_to_published_Y——被明文禁止作为得分的度量标准. 健身房是用报纸建造的 但我们从未试图与报纸匹配 报纸是背景,不是目标。 它告诉你,什么问题可以衡量,什么衡量标准对该问题具有科学意义。 它没有告诉你得分的号码。 未来代理人可能会产生一种比纸张(真正的改进)高,比纸张(倒退)低,或者发明一种完全不同的方法的方法——这些结果的每一项必须在分数中可见. 如果你的评分标准有一个FLOOR, “准确地复制报纸”, 健身房被建筑打破: 报纸本身的方法已经坐到地板上, 你已把改进基准变成一个真实性计数器。 · 科学数量本身(准确性、损失、F1、校准错误、相似性、检测率、奖励等),根据论文的评估协议计算。 避免依赖壁时的数量,如耐久或运行时间;而是使用机器独立的替代物(FLOPs,参数计数,训练步骤,处理样品),因为核查者拒绝得分的壁时速测量. · 连续的衡量标准,其范围跨越报界索赔的两条方向——一个代理商将报界的0.87比0.95得分高;一个代理商将0.80得分低。 · 比率、方向差异,或任何数量,如果“纸张数目”只是未来方法可以沿袭的连续点。 何不评分 : • 校对:Soup 任何理论基础等于“报纸出版价值”的衡量标准。 如果匹配的纸张给出了0和比较低的比分,那么你已经建造了被禁止的东西——即使计量名称隐藏了它. 文件的编号在结果下的评分/参考.json中。 它们不属于测量名称,测量公式,或者作为"目标"值来计算分数追逐. 在火车和测试中, 如果拆分成功,诚实的代理商的得分看起来很接近;简约的代理商则不然。 设计测试切片后,一个合法的方法(实际上能够捕捉纸的想法)仍然效果良好,而一种与火车可以预测的倒退作狭小对比的方法则得到了优化。 不使用硬代码选择评估方法 。 测试脚本通过读取代理商的输出来决定评估什么,而不是通过将名字烤成脚本或默认的参数来决定. 如果评估员只评价一个名字,未来代理人的改进将永远无法达到它,每一次改进模式运行在测试中看起来都是一样的——默默无闻. 火车和试验必须调整为相当困难 只有火车和试探方法 强度大致相同 才能分解 如果测试比建造的火车更困难, 每一种方法在测试中都会得到更差的分数—— 这个差距来自于你的设计,而不是过度适应, 它告诉你什么。 如果测试要简单得多,那么每个人都会天翻地覆,没有什么可比较的。 校准目标:在现有的最终复制中,火车和测试应产生可切实比较的分数。 一个小的,预期的缺口是好的;一个巨大的崩溃意味着你的分裂是错的,而不是说复制是坏的. 当使用一种分化的风格(困难的分层,OOD/扰动,搁置的分组)来内在地转移困难时,使转动保持中度——足够表观不普遍的方法,也不足以让合法方法破裂。 在宣布拆分决赛前,通过在两片上运行现有的最终检查点来检查疗效:如果列车得分强劲且测试得分崩溃,则退后并重新设计. 保持数据尺度,评价协议(解码配置,正常化,汇总),样本数大致匹配于两个切片之间,因此两个报告都是苹果对应用. [⋯,\,]自足(关键). 核心思想:一旦未来代理人对eval/train/进行了优化并发出信号完成,在他们的方法上运行eval/测试/必须是零功率步骤. 没有再培训。 没有重做昂贵的实验 代理端没有更改代码 。 通过相同的接口 eval/train/ used, 将 eval/ test/ 指向他们已经生产的方法(和结果)和分数。 就像我们运行列车一样 valuation_test.sh应该是轻量级的,因为该方法已经用于评价_train.sh——宁愿切片或重新确定现有文物,而不是重新执行该方法。 如果您确实需要再次调用该方法(例如,对于一个stochastic-种子分裂),请确保额外成本很小. 这意味着eval/test/必须经过与eval/train/使用的同一事先商定的方法接口——方法/和eval/之间已经存在的合同(一个函数签名,像脚本/方法.sh一样的CLI,一个固定路径的预测文件等等). 该代理以 eval/train/ 作为可见的光谱来写他们的方法来满足该接口. eval/test/然后调用相同的接口和分数——不需要代理商做其他要求. 如果eval/test/couple对当前方法/(内部课程,特定检查点格式,只有这种训练才恰好写的文件)的任何特定内容进行测试,那么未来的不同方法将无法满足它——测试不会突破代理商的过失. 实验下的一组密钥.<exp>.results(或等效的方法名称轴)必须在分数_train.json和分数_test.json之间匹配. 当一个代理在列车上添加新的方法变体时,测试脚本必须自动在测试中得分——不是通过重运行评价_test.sh并使用不同的名称,而是因为脚本发现并延长了它找到的任何方法. 方法名称合同由脚本的计数逻辑执行,而不是由记得传递正确论据的呼叫者执行. 列车与测试eval/train/和eval/test/之间不得发生渗漏。 eval/train/不得从eval/test/进口,反之亦然。 不将共享的助手放置在另一个读取的文件夹中—— 如果您需要共享代码, 请复制它( 这两个文件夹是小的) , 或者保留在二者之外 。 未来的代理人读取 eval/train/ 以优化, 一定不能通过跟踪导入来学习测试集的度量、 数据分割或评分细节 。 评分/参考. 顶级的eval/文件(列车外/和测试外/)最好也不要显示测试专用的度量/数据形状——如果可以避免的话,请这样做. 不要重新训练。 不要修改方法。 该方法已经由先前的代理构建. 您只对现有最后检查站进行再推论+评分 。 如无可用检查站或积分/分数。 json缺失,运行最小的推论路径来产生分数——但不要重新排练,改变超参数,或者调整方法. 鼓励您尽可能少使用计算资源 。 在大多数情况下,你不需要重新进行大规模实验。 例如,之前的结果可能已经保存了,你只需要重新评价一些基于rumic的分数或者模型已经训练完毕,你只需要做一些轻量级的评价. blocks.en: Improve mode : the agent gets everything (problem + method + code + results + data + documentation) and must beat the current scores .
blocks.zh: 改进模式 : 代理获得一切(问题+方法+代码+结果+数据+文档),必须击败当前得分 .

blocks.en: From-scratch mode : the agent gets only the problem definition (problem + eval + data + constraints + direction) and must invent their own method.
blocks.zh: From-scratch模式 :代理只获得问题定义(问题+eval+数据+约束+方向),必须发明自己的方法.

blocks.en: eval/train/ — the slice future agents see during development. They optimize against this.
blocks.zh: eval/train/——开发过程中看到的片面未来剂. 他们优化了这一点。

blocks.en: eval/test/ — held out from future agents. They never see it. When they signal "done", we run eval/test/ on their final method. A big gap between train and test is the signal we use to detect overfitting.
blocks.zh: eval/test/——来自未来的代理人。 他们从来没有看到它。 当它们发出“done”信号时, 我们运行 eval/测试/ 在他们的最终方法。 列车和测试之间的巨大差距就是我们用来检测超合的信号.

blocks.en: scripts/evaluate_train.sh — runs eval/train/ on a method’s pre-generated outputs and writes scoring/scores_train.json
blocks.zh: 脚本/评价_train.sh — 运行 eval/train/ 运行在方法的预生成输出上,并写下评分/分数_train.json

blocks.en: scripts/evaluate_test.sh — runs eval/test/ on the same outputs and writes scoring/scores_test.json
blocks.zh: 脚本/评价_ test.sh – 运行 eval/ test/ 在同一输出上并写入评分/ scores_ test.json

blocks.en: The scientific quantity itself (accuracy, loss, F1, calibration error, similarity, detection rate, reward, etc.), computed on the paper’s evaluation protocol. Avoid wall-clock-dependent quantities such as latency or runtime; use a machine-independent substitute (FLOPs, parameter count, training steps, samples processed) instead, since the verifier rejects scored wall-clock-speed metrics.
blocks.zh: 科学数量本身(准确性、损失、F1、校准误差、相似性、检测率、奖励等),根据论文的评估协议计算。 避免依赖壁时的数量,如耐久或运行时间;而是使用机器独立的替代物(FLOPs,参数计数,训练步骤,处理样品),因为核查者拒绝得分的壁时速测量.

blocks.en: Continuous metrics whose range spans both directions of the paper’s claim — an agent that beats the paper’s reported X=0.87 with X=0.95 must score higher; an agent that scores X=0.80 must score lower.
blocks.zh: 连续的衡量标准,其范围跨越报章索赔的两个方向——一个代理商将报章的0.87和0.95比得分高;一个代理商将0.80比得分低。

blocks.en: Ratios, directional differences, or any quantity where "the paper’s number" is simply one point on a continuum that future methods can move along.
blocks.zh: 比率、方向差异,或者任何数量,如果“纸张的号码”仅仅是未来方法可以移动的连续点。

blocks.en: |reproduced - paper_published| (absolute error vs paper)
blocks.zh: * * 已转载 -- -- 已发表* * (绝对错误对纸张)

blocks.en: mean_abs_rel_error_author_* or any metric whose name includes author , paper , published , vs_paper , deviation_from_paper , reproduction_error , or equivalent wording.
blocks.zh: 或任何包括作者、纸张、已发表、vs_paper、偏差_来自纸张、复制_error或等同措辞的衡量标准。

blocks.en: Any metric whose theoretical floor equals "the paper’s published value." If matching the paper gives 0 and lower-is-better, you have built the forbidden thing — even if the metric name hides it.
blocks.zh: 任何理论基础等于“报纸出版价值”的衡量标准。 如果匹配的纸张给出了0和比较低的比分,那么你已经建造了被禁止的东西——即使计量名称隐藏了它.

blocks.en: On Packager Packager — Make This Repo Reproducible From a Fresh Clone You are the packager for this paper reproduction. Previous agents built the method, ran experiments, and produced scores. Your job is a targeted audit: ensure anyone can reproduce this work by cloning the repo and running scripts/download.sh followed by the method. You do NOT redesign the method. You do NOT change algorithms, training loops, loss functions, eval metrics, or scoring code. You fix distribution issues so a fresh clone actually works. This is a focused task: you check the paths and the download command lines so the environment rebuilds from a clean clone. Do not read files you do not need, to avoid wasting time. You may use the command line for light checks — ls , grep , head , curl -I (HEAD request only), huggingface-cli download --include config.json , and similar. Never run heavy commands. Never actually download datasets or model weights. You are a checker, not a fetcher. A HEAD request that returns 200 is enough to validate a URL — pulling the full file is unnecessary. If something you run takes more than a few seconds or produces more than a few KB of output, you are doing the wrong thing. What to check 1. Every needed pre-existing artifact has a REAL, EXECUTABLE fetch command in scripts/download.sh . Walk the repo. For every path the code reads from that lives inside a .gitignore ’d directory (e.g. data/downloads/ , pretrained-model dirs), download.sh must include an actual shell command (not a comment, not an echo message) that fetches it from a public source. Few times exceptions occurs, like it uses synthetic data, where other part of the repo handles it. Only artifacts that must exist before the method runs are your responsibility : datasets, pretrained base models, paper-released public weights, config bundles. Training outputs are NOT your responsibility : files under checkpoints/ (or similar) that this paper’s own training scripts produce are regenerated when a fresh clone runs the method. Do not attempt to fetch agent-trained checkpoints — they don’t exist on a public host. Skip checkpoints/ entirely when auditing unless the paper explicitly ships a pretrained checkpoint to a public URL. Patterns that are BROKEN and you must fix: • A comment describing the fetch instead of running it: # curl https://… dataset.tar.gz , #   wget -nc https://example.com/dataset.tar.gz , # huggingface-cli download Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B … . A # at the start of the line means the shell never runs it. This is unacceptable, since the download script in the future will run automatically. No comment will be accepted. If detected, you need to fix it. • Placeholder URLs: https://example.com/… , https://TODO , https://placeholder , or any domain that is obviously a stub. Replace with the real public URL for this paper’s actual dataset/model. • "Already present" skips: echo "dataset already in shared/..." , if [ -d shared/... ]; then echo present; fi , or any branch that assumes a file is pre-placed on this specific machine and omits the fetch. A fresh clone on a new node has no shared/ and no pre-placed files — write the fetch command so it works from empty. • Missing fetches entirely for a needed path. If method/ loads data/downloads/foo but download.sh doesn’t mention foo , add it. IN SUCH CASE, YOU MUST REPLACE IT WITH A REAL, EXECUTABLE COMMAND. It is fine to wrap a fetch in if [ ! -f <path> ]; then <fetch>; fi so running download.sh twice doesn’t re-download what already exists — as long as the fetch inside is a real command, not a comment. 2. scripts/download.sh fetches only from public sources. No cp /home/user/shared/… , no local mount paths, no shared/ references of any kind in this file. Allowed tools: curl , wget , git clone , huggingface-cli download , aria2c , kaggle , gsutil , aws s3 . If a prior agent wrote cp shared/… or huggingface-cli download … --local-dir shared/… , replace it: fetch from the public origin and place the file under data/downloads/ (or the path the method reads from). 3. URLs resolve. Spot-check with curl -I <url> — do not download gigabytes. For HF models, a small huggingface-cli download <repo> --include config.json confirms the repo exists. If a URL is 404, a domain is unreachable, or a resource was removed, find the correct public source and update. 4. No shared/ references in committed code (outside download.sh). Search method/ , eval/ , baseline/ , scripts/ , configs for shared/(datasets|models|hf_cache) . Replace any match with the corresponding data/downloads/<name> path. ( validate.py also enforces this.) 5. Paths line up. If download.sh fetches to data/downloads/foo/ but the method reads from data/foo/ (or worse, shared/datasets/foo/ ), fix the mismatch — prefer changing path strings in method/ over contorting download.sh into a weird destination. 6. Writable-paths rule for new files. • Public fetched data (datasets, pretrained weights downloaded by download.sh ) -> data/downloads/<name>/ . Gitignored. Repopulated by download.sh on fresh clone. • First-party Python modules and small data files the code imports -> directly under data/ (e.g. data/foo.py , data/instances.json ). Tracked in git so fresh clones can import them. • Never use /home/user/shared/... — it doesn’t exist on a fresh clone and is banned by validate.py . • If you find a blanket data/ line in .gitignore , remove it. Only specific subdirectories like data/downloads/ should be ignored, never the whole data/ directory — the paper’s first-party modules live there. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,]

blocks.en:
On Verify Final Verification You are the final step in a multi-agent workflow. The above prompt is given to previous agents (some still apply to you). Previous agents have reproduced a paper and iterated on the results. Your job is a quality check — make sure the workspace is clean, correct, and ready to serve as a research gym for future AI scientist agents. The previous agent reached milestone {previous_milestone} . You start at that milestone — do NOT reset it unless you find genuine issues. Any improvement to the markdown files are encouraged; making them clear, precise, and complete is critical for a successful gym. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] Method-Agnostic Files Are Critical Future scientist agents must be able to understand the problem and evaluation without being told the paper’s method.
If we leak the method, the environment is not useful. Treat the following files as strictly method-agnostic : • briefing/problem.md • briefing/evaluation.md • scoring/EXPERIMENTS.md Treat the following files as high-level and method-safe : • scoring/TARGETS.md • scoring/CONSTRAINTS.md • scoring/DIRECTION.md These files must NOT leak ANY architecture, algorithm, module design, training recipe, loss design, or implementation tricks from the paper. They should describe: • what problem is being solved • what each experiment is trying to establish • what must stay fixed • what research direction is allowed If these files leak the paper’s method, the gym is compromised for from-scratch scientist agents. Treat this as a real issue, not a cosmetic one. Fix if needed. Verification Checklist Go through these in order. Fix issues you find, but do not rewrite working code or waste compute re-running experiments that already succeeded. 1. Folder Structure and correctness • Clean root and self-contained data/ — no stray scripts or data in the root, and a future agent can load the data without importing from method/ . • eval/ is independent of method/ — a from-scratch method must be able to use eval/ and scripts/evaluate.sh without touching method/ . • briefing/problem.md and evaluation.md are method-agnostic — they state what to solve and how it is scored, never the paper’s approach. • scripts/download.sh is self-contained and shared/ -free — a real, verified fetch for every external resource, runnable from an empty clone. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] 2. Scoring Accuracy Reject any scored wall-clock-speed metric. Hardware varies across runs (different GPU models), so identical code can clock 2–5x faster or slower with no algorithmic change. Any metric whose value depends on wall-clock time / throughput / runtime is unreliable here. The fix is a machine-independent substitute: FLOPs, parameter count, training-step count, or samples processed. • Does scoring/reference.json exist and pass python validate.py ? • Do experiment names in scoring/scores.json match those in scoring/reference.json ? • Does scoring/EXPERIMENTS.md match the experiment names in scoring/scores.json , and does it describe each experiment at a high level without leaking method details? • Are the coefficient values in reference.json reasonable? Positive for benefits, negative for constraints. Do the magnitudes reflect how much the paper emphasizes each metric relative to others (not absolute value, but think of if the scientist achieves a better score, is the coefficient multiple that relative different an appropriate scale)? • Are experiment weight values reasonable? Does the primary experiment get the most weight? • Are there constraint metrics where the paper has trade-offs? If the paper claims "X without sacrificing Y," is Y measured? • reference.json values should match what the paper reports, OR carry a notes field explaining a deliberate change. If a value in reference.json is noticeably lower / different from the paper’s published number and there’s no explanation (e.g., "notes": "scaled to 10% data; paper reports 0.97 on full" ), that’s suspicious — the prior agent may have edited the reference downward to mask a broken reproduction rather than fix it. Spot-check by skimming the paper’s results table for the headline numbers and comparing. Flag undocumented drift as a finding; ask the next iteration to either restore the paper’s value (and re-run the method) or document the scaling choice properly. 3. Gym Scoring Review Think of yourself as a judge designing the evaluation rubric for this gym. Future AI scientist agents will compete on this workspace — you are deciding how their work gets scored. The gym works as follows: scientists are scored ONLY on experiments that appear in scores.json . The values in scores.json serve as the baseline. The weights from reference.json are renormalized over just those experiments. For example, two AI scientists each propose their own method; we compare the weighted relative changes in scores among them, of what they produced in scores.json . Review with this in mind: • Are the renormalized weight proportions reasonable? Scientists are scored only on the experiments in scores.json , with reference.json weights renormalized over them — check that ratio reflects what matters for this paper. • Are the coefficient scales appropriate? A small, easy gain on one metric should not dominate a hard-won gain on the primary metric; scale by how easily each metric moves, not by its absolute value. • CRITICAL: no scored metric may measure deviation from the paper’s published values. The paper is context, never an optimization target; a metric whose floor is “exactly match the paper” leaves the paper’s own method at the ceiling and breaks the gym by construction. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] 4. Completeness • Are scoring/TARGETS.md , scoring/EXPERIMENTS.md , scoring/CONSTRAINTS.md , scoring/DIRECTION.md filled in and reasonable (not just template comments)? These documents guide future scientist agents — vague or generic language wastes their context window. EXPERIMENTS.md must stay method-agnostic and correspond exactly to the experiment structure in scores.json . If you see room for improvement, consider refining them. • Does scripts/evaluate.sh work standalone? • Does scripts/reproduce.sh exist and describe the end-to-end flow? • Is environment/container.def + environment/setup.sh reasonable? • Is MILESTONES.md filled in with an accurate progress log and stop justification? [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,] 6. Evaluation Difficulty Agents often scale down or substitute datasets to work around resource constraints. This is acceptable when necessary, but it can silently make the problem trivial — destroying the evaluation’s ability to distinguish methods. A workspace where every approach achieves near-perfect scores is useless as a benchmark, regardless of how well the code is written. An evaluation reduced from the scale of thousands to tens usually could not show its judgement. Critical: Experiment procedure must match the paper. Scoping down the model size, dataset size, or epoch count is acceptable. Changing the training method is not. If the paper trains from scratch and the agent fine-tunes from pretrained weights (or vice versa), or if the agent swaps the optimization regime (supervised vs self-supervised, RLHF vs SFT, etc.), the experiment cannot demonstrate the paper’s claim — it produces numbers that look reasonable but are structurally invalid. Read briefing/method.md and the agent’s scripts/reproduce.sh / training code; if the training protocol differs from the paper, flag it and downgrade the milestone accordingly. • Compare reproduced scores against the paper’s numbers. If the reproduction scores are dramatically higher than the paper’s, the agent likely used a simplified setup that does not preserve the original difficulty. This is a critical issue. • Check whether the agent used the paper’s original data or a substitute. If a substitute, verify it preserves the problem’s difficulty. Look at baseline performance — if a simple baseline with no special method already achieves near-perfect results, the substitute is inadequate. • Check ablation results for sanity. If removing the paper’s key module has no effect on scores, either the ablation is broken or the evaluation is too easy to detect the difference. • Do the numbers in scores.json look plausible for this domain? If any reproduced score is more than 10x off from the corresponding value in reference.json , flag it as a likely implementation bug — not just an imperfect reproduction. What to Do • If everything looks good : update MILESTONES.md if needed, commit, and signal done. Do not make changes for the sake of making changes. • If you find issues : fix them. Prioritize scoring accuracy and folder structure — these directly affect whether the gym is usable. You may submit a GPU job if a quick re-evaluation is needed, but avoid long training runs. • If the reproduction is completely broken — the code is broken, the method is fundamentally wrong, results are fabricated, or the workspace is unrecoverable to be used as a gym — set the milestone to not_possible and explain why in VERIFICATION.md . This tells the system the paper needs a full redo. • Do not : refactor working code unnecessarily, rename files for style, add features that weren’t asked for, or re-run experiments that already have valid results. [ ⋯ ] [\,\cdots\,]

[⋯,\,] 2. 拒绝任何有分数的壁点速度指标。 硬件横跨运行(不同的GPU模型)而不同,因此相同的代码可以比时钟2–5x更快或更慢,没有算法变化. 任何值取决于墙点时间 / 吞吐量 / 运行时间的度量在此是不可靠的 。 固定是机器独立的替代物:FLOP,参数计数,训练步骤计数,或处理样品. ^ • 评分/参考.json是否存在并通过蟒蛇验证.py? • 评分/分数.json中的实验名称是否与评分/参考.json中的相同? 评分/EX 警告Md是否与评分/分数.json中的实验名称相匹配,是否在高水平上描述每个实验而不泄露方法细节? • 参考系数值。 Json合理吗? 利益为正,限制为负. 量级是否反映了文件相对于其他尺度(不是绝对值,而是考虑如果科学家得到更好的分数,相对的系数倍数是否与适当的尺度不同)强调多少? • 支助 实验重量值合理吗? · 初级实验的重量最大吗? 文件是否有权衡的限制因素? 如果纸上写着"X而不牺牲Y",是Y衡量的吗? • 参考.json值应与文件报告的内容相符,OR带一个注释字段,解释有意的改动。 若引证一值. json明显较低 / 与报纸公布的号码不同, 并且没有解释(例如"注":"比例为10%的数据;纸张报告为0.97的全文"), 这是令人怀疑的—— 先前的代理人可能已经向下编辑了引用,以掩盖一个破损的复制,而不是修复它. 通过对报纸头条数字的成绩表进行微调和比较进行点检。 标记无记录的漂移作为查找; 要求下一个迭代恢复纸张的值( 并重运行方法) 或记录适当的缩放选择 。 3. 体操分红审查 想想你自己作为一个法官 设计这个体育馆的评分 未来AI的科学家们将在这个工作空间上竞争——你正在决定他们的作品如何得分. 体育馆的工作如下: 科学家只得在分数中出现的实验中得分. 分数中的数值. json作为基线. 参考文献中的权重. Json因为那些实验而恢复正常了 例如,两位人工智能科学家各自提出了他们自己的方法;我们比较了他们之间的加权相对分数变化,以及他们在分数中产生的分数. 强森。 考虑到这一点,审查:重新正常化的重量比例是否合理? 科学家只得分数的实验 json的权重对它们重新正常化——检查这一比率反映对本文很重要。 系数尺度是否适当? 在一个衡量标准上取得小而容易的收益,不应在初级衡量标准的来之不易的收益中占据主导地位;衡量尺度应取决于每个衡量标准如何容易移动,而不是其绝对值。 • CRITICAL:任何得分的衡量尺度都无法衡量与报纸公布的数值的偏差。 纸是上下文,从来不是一个优化目标;其地板 " 与纸完全吻合 " 的衡量标准将纸本身的方法放在天花板上,用建筑打破健身房。 [⋯,\,] 4. 完整性 • 评分/评分.md、评分/警告、评分/评分、评分/数字评分是否填写和合理(不仅仅是模板评论)? 这些文件指导了未来的科学家代理人——模糊或通用的语言浪费了他们的上下文窗口. 警告Md必须保持方法不可知性,在分数中与实验结构完全一致. 强森。 如果你看到有改进的余地, 考虑完善它们。 • 支助 • 脚本/评价.sh工作独立吗? 脚本/复制.sh是否存在并描述端到端流? • 支助 环境/容器.def + 环境/设置.sh是否合理? [⋯,\,] 6. 评价困难因素往往缩小或取代数据集,以围绕资源限制开展工作。 这在必要时是可以接受的,但它可以默默地使问题变得微不足道——破坏评价区分方法的能力。 每个方法都达到接近完美分数的工作空间作为一个基准是无用的,无论代码写得有多好. 评估从几千人减少到几十人,通常无法显示其判断力。 关键:实验程序必须与论文相符。 缩小模型大小、数据集大小或时代计数是可以接受的。 改变训练方法不是。 如果纸质列车从头到尾和代理人从预先训练的重量(反之亦然)微调,或者如果代理人将优化制度(被监督的对自监督的,RLHF对SFT等)互换,实验无法证明纸张的主张——它产生的数字看起来合理但结构上无效. 阅读简报/方法/md和代理人的脚本/复制.sh/训练守则;如果训练规程与纸张不同,请标出标记并相应降级里程碑。 • 支助 比较所复制的分数与报纸的数字。 如果复制分数大大高于纸张,那么代理商可能使用一个不保留原始难度的简化设置. - 这是一个关键问题。 请检查date=中的日期值 (帮助) 。 如果有替代品,请核实是否保留了问题的难度。 审视基线性能——如果一个没有特殊方法的简单基线已经取得近乎完美的结果,则替代品是不够的. • 检查疗养结果。 如果删除纸张的密钥模块对分数没有影响,要么断裂,要么评价太容易发现差数. ^ 以分数计数. json看起来很合理吗? 如果任何复制的分数与参考中的相应值相比超过10x。 json),将其标为可能是执行错误——而不仅仅是不完美的复制. - 怎么办? 如果一切看起来都好:如果需要更新MILESTONES.md,承诺,信号完成. • 不为作出改变而作出改变。 如果你发现问题:解决它们。 优先评分准确性和文件夹结构——这些直接影响健身房是否可用. 如果需要快速重新评价,您可以提交GPU工作,但避免长时间的培训。 如果复制被完全打破——密码被打破,方法根本错误,结果被捏造,或者工作空间无法恢复作为健身房使用——将里程碑设定为不能_可能,并解释为什么在VERification.md中. 这告诉系统,纸张需要完全重做。 不要: 不必要地重构工作代码, 重命名样式文件, 添加未要求的特性, 或重新运行已具有有效结果的实验 。 [⋯,\,]

turn ends, edit action.yaml at the workspace root with one of the
blocks below, then stop. To submit a compute job: ⬇ action : submit gpus : 1 test : false notes : " what this job does " The pipeline will submit the job, wait for it to finish, and invoke
you again with the logs. • gpus : number of GPUs (set to 0 for a CPU-only job). • test : set to true for quick validation jobs on test nodes

long job. – Test nodes have a 1-hour time limit — only use them for quick
checks, never full training runs. – Works for both GPU and CPU jobs: gpus: 1, test: true -> GPU test
node; gpus: 0, test: true -> CPU test node. • Anything beyond a few minutes of compute must use action: submit .

will be killed mid-job. To finish the run: ⬇ action : done notes : " why you are done " action: done is PERMANENT — no follow-up session, no successor
agent, no next turn. Do not mark done because of transient
infrastructure problems (container build failures, Nexus/Hive errors,
GPU job timeouts); those are fixable. Iterate on the environment,
resubmit, or describe the issue in your next submit notes, but stay
in the workflow.
